_comment: The people at The Landing. Six of them, standing around a field on a Saturday. They carry the campaign: every chapter's brief and closer is delivered by somebody who has an opinion about it. Written as a design artifact, same as the enemy chatter bank.
_writingRules: Nobody explains a mechanic. They have opinions about it, and the opinion contains the mechanic.
No profanity, no slurs, no threats. Roblox Mild, and it is funnier clean.
No firearm words, ever. Markers, hoppers, barrels, air, paint, fill.
Everyone wants something and nobody is a quest dispenser. Marge wants the field to survive another season. Tildy wants someone to let her test things.
The player never speaks aloud -- dialogue options are what you chose to say, not a voice. It keeps the walk quiet.
Dark, not bleak. The dread is economic and social: a business quietly failing, a man narrating his life to nobody, forty years spent on one hobby. Never harm.

Denny is the only one who talks like the internet. That is the joke and it only works because nobody else does -- Marge asking him what a word means is funnier than six people using it. Do not spread his voice to the others.

marge.role: Owns the field. Runs the counter.
marge.voice: Dry. Forty years of this. Has seen every kind of person walk through that door and has stopped being surprised by any of them.
marge._outfit: Flannel, apron, readers on her head, clipboard. The only person here dressed for a job.

tildy.role: Chrono, air, and the fun stuff.
tildy.greeting: Okay so I have been thinking.
tildy.voice: Nineteen, over-caffeinated, genuinely brilliant with a wrench, absolutely should not be allowed near the drone.
tildy._outfit: Goggles up, headphones down, bandolier of pods she does not need, drone controller already clipped on.

wheels.role: Marker tech. Lives in the truck bay.
wheels.voice: Obsessive. Will explain dwell to anyone who stands still. Has never once been wrong about a marker.
wheels._outfit: Coveralls, thigh tool roll, headlamp on in daylight, one boot untied.

coachRuiz.greeting: Show me the last ten shots.
coachRuiz.voice: Was regional-level in the nineties. Quiet, precise, entirely uninterested in how you feel about your performance.
coachRuiz._outfit: The nineties team jersey, whistle, stopwatch, backwards cap, one knee brace older than the knee.

denny.greeting: Hey. Hey. Did you see that?
denny.voice: One of the six you keep eliminating. Bears no grudge whatsoever. Delighted to be here. Comic relief and, occasionally, an accidentally excellent tip.
denny._outfit: Night vision flipped DOWN, in daylight, for rec league. Everything at once. This is the joke.

theMarshal.voice: Never speaks. Communicates entirely in gestures at the notice board. Unlocks horde by simply walking to the back gate and holding it open.
theMarshal._outfit: A white armband and nothing else, on a field where everyone is wearing three hundred dollars of nylon.

_dialogue: Trees keyed by npc. Each node has lines, and options that either move to another node, fire an action, or end. `requires` gates a node or an option on campaign state, so the same NPC says different things as you progress -- which is the whole point of having them.

lines: You again.
Field's open. Same as it was yesterday. Same as it'll be tomorrow, probably.

options.text: What's in the case behind you?

lines: {chapterBrief}
Mm.
Gate's where it's always been. It's not going to move because you agreed to something.
That's not for sale.
It's a pump. Gold. Twelve in the hopper and a barrel somebody cut by hand in 2003.
I've had four people ask to buy it. I told all four the same thing.
It's the worst marker on this field. One shot, then you work the pump, and if you missed, you missed.
Anyone who wants it because it's gold can't use it. Anyone who can use it doesn't care that it's gold.
So it sits there. Like everything else here.
Timed run. Same building, same doors, and a clock that does not care how you feel about any of it.
Denny's done it four hundred times. Denny has not improved.

options.text: Why does he keep doing it?

lines: Because the clock's honest. Nothing else out here is.
You can lie to yourself about a match. Six people, bad angles, somebody's kid on the wrong team.
You cannot lie to a stopwatch. That's the whole appeal and it's also why most people only do it once.
You did the thing.
All four fields. Pro. Nobody touched you.
So. The case.
Take it. It's yours, it's terrible, and you've earned the right to find that out personally.
Case stays. Case has been there longer than you have.
Mm.
Okay so I have been thinking.
Which Marge says is the dangerous part.
Pods. Everyone buys the six-pack, right? Six pods, never run dry, brilliant.
Except you're carrying a shelf. You sound like a shelf. They hear the shelf coming.
Get the racer harness. Three pods, mounted tight, and you reload like it's nothing.
It's not! That's the trade! You get fewer and you get them faster!
Nothing here is better than anything else, it's all just -- differently annoying.
Marge says that's the whole business model. Marge says that about everything.
Marge said it about my birthday.
RIGHT. Okay. So it does not see through walls.
Everyone asks. It does not. I could build one that did and Marge would put me in the pond.
What it does is listen. Anyone who's fired in the last few seconds, it works out roughly where they are and puts a mark on it.
It's very good ears! On a stick! That flies!
And before you ask — yes, the shots you take while it's up get flagged.
Coach won't score them for crosshair placement. He was extremely clear about that.
It is the loudest thing I have ever built.
Every single one of them knows exactly where you are the second it lifts.
So, you know. Use it somewhere you're about to leave.
Bye! Come back! I have ideas!
Don't touch that, it's timed.
Everything in here is timed. That's the job.
Dwell. Valve's open four milliseconds too long, so it's burning air and throwing hot.
Nobody notices. Everybody notices at forty metres.
That's most of my life, that sentence.
Ball's in the air over a third of a second. Drops the better part of a metre.
So you're not aiming at them, you're aiming at a spot above them, and if the velocity wanders you're aiming at a spot that moved.
Consistent air. That's the whole job. Forty years, that's the whole job.
Depends what you're bad at, and I've watched you.
Mech's honest. Electro wins rooms and loses treelines. Pump makes you commit and pays you for it.
None of them shoot straighter than the others. Anyone who tells you different is selling something.
She'll tell you she's closing. She's been closing since 2011.
She had the sign made. It's in the loft. I know because I put it there.
Ask her about the sign sometime. Actually, don't.
Mm-hm. Timed.
Show me the last ten shots.
I'll know in four.
{prescription}
Because missing and under-leading are not the same mistake and they do not have the same fix.
If your angle is good and your lead is short, you don't need to aim better. You need to aim somewhere else.
Most people spend a year not knowing which one they're doing. Some people spend a career.
A career.
Eleven years. I was quick and I was wrong, and quick and wrong looks exactly like good until somebody films it.
Somebody filmed it.
The sign. If your misses are all on the same side of them, that's lead -- you're shooting where they were.
If they're scattered evenly, that's not lead, that's drop, and you want the holdover boards.
The range keeps the sign. That's the only reason it's worth anything, and it's the only reason I'm still here.
Boards are always up. I'm always here. Neither of those is a threat.
Hey. Hey. Did you see that?

options.text: Aren't you on the other team?

lines: Nothing. There was a heron. It's gone now.
Anyway -- you got me in round three. Straight through the gap on the snake side. I was so cooked.
I've been thinking about it a lot actually. Like, a normal amount. Like a normal amount for a person.
Oh, no, it was great! Genuinely! You ate.
I told everyone. Oz doesn't believe me. Oz thinks I'm being delulu about it.
I said Oz, I was THERE.
You waited. That's the thing. You waited until Marcus committed and then you took the angle he left.
We can't cover two lanes with the same guy. Nobody can. It just LOOKS like we can because there's six of us.
...I probably shouldn't have said that. Chat, I probably shouldn't have said that.
What? Nobody. It's a figure of speech.
...I don't stream. I keep saying I'm going to. I bought the light.
The light's still in the box. In my car. It's been in my car since March.
Yeah.
Yeah, okay. See you out there. Please don't lead with the snake.
Yeah! No, yeah. I'm on the squad.
But like, off the field we're all just guys. Marcus does my taxes. Badly, but he does them.
It's not that deep.
Later! Get home safe! ...you live here basically, but still!
She looks at you.
Then at the notice board.
Then back at you.
This is the entire conversation and she is fully committed to it.
She taps the third column with one finger. Times. Full clears, all five rounds.
Then she shrugs, very slightly. It is somehow worse than being told.
She turns and walks to the back gate.
She points to a sign: Horde -- coming later.
There is no round counter on the sign above it. She taps the empty space twice.
She nods, once.
It is the warmest thing that has happened to you today.

_entryNote: A node with entry:true is an alternate OPENING for that npc, chosen over root when its requires are met. A node with only `requires` is still just a gated sub-node reached from somewhere else -- Tildy's drone talk is gated but you still get to it by asking her about it.
_outfitNote: Each person's outfit lives in Data/wardrobe.json under the same id. Written against the `voice` field above it -- the clothes are supposed to be the same joke as the dialogue.
_shoothouseNote: Marge explains the course because it is the one mode a new player meets before the field has a squad on it, and a timed mode that nobody explains reads as a bug rather than a discipline. She does not sell it -- the medals are not a reward she hands out, which is the point of them.
